documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine f/u. Fully vaccinated for COVID now. Got through winter without getting sick. Still walking, now outside again. BP log 118-134/68-80. Denies CP, dyspnea, orthopnea, swelling, foot numbness.
Meds: no changes, taking all.
O: Comfortable. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. No pedal edema.
A/P:
- DM2: A1c and BMP drawn. Metformin 1000 BID.
- HTN: controlled.
- CKD 3b: creatinine today.
- CAD: no angina.
- Wants to switch everything to 90-day mail order, will send new scripts.
Follow up June, can be video.

documents.title: A1c and BMP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 6.8, down from 7.7 in September. Potassium and creatinine stable. Portal note sent, no changes.

documents.title: Mail order pharmacy call
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Mail-order pharmacy called; they received 90-day scripts for 4 of 5 meds but nothing for the metoprolol. Checked, it was sent to his local pharmacy by mistake in March. Resent metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg #90 with 3 refills to mail order per PCP standing refill protocol. Called patient, he has about 10 days left locally, told him to pick up a fill there to bridge.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, he is at home at the kitchen table, wife helped with the tablet. Verbal consent for telehealth.
No new concerns. Home BPs this month 120s/70s. Fasting sugars on his meter mostly 120-150. Mail order working now. No chest pain or shortness of breath walking 2 miles. No lightheadedness.
Meds unchanged.
Assessment: HTN, DM2, CKD 3b, CAD all stable by report.
Plan: Wellness visit in September with fasting labs. Eye exam reminder again; he made an appointment for August.

documents.title: Optometry diabetic eye exam
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Diabetic Eye Examination Report
Date of exam: 08/12/2021
Patient: Howard Marino

Dilated fundus examination, both eyes. Visual acuity with correction 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS. Intraocular pressures within normal limits. Lens: early age-appropriate changes, not visually significant. Fundus: optic discs healthy, maculae flat, no microaneurysms, hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization in either eye.

Impression: No diabetic retinopathy OU.
Recommendation: repeat dilated exam in 1-2 years. New glasses prescription given.

Allergies: NKDA.
Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT (initial)

Health risk assessment reviewed with patient. Lives with wife in a two-story house, bedroom upstairs, no trouble with stairs. Independent with all daily activities, still drives, does the yard. No falls in the past year. Hearing fine per him, wife disagrees mildly; he declines audiology for now. Vision: eye exam in August, no retinopathy, new glasses. Sleeps 7 hours.

Depression screen PHQ-2: 0.
Cognition: Mini-Cog 5/5.
Activity: walks 30-40 min most days.
Diet: wife cooks, cutting back on bread and pasta 'mostly'.

Medications reviewed, no changes. No OTC NSAIDs.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP and weight reviewed. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Feet normal, monofilament intact bilaterally, pulses good.

Screening/prevention plan:
- Colon: colonoscopy 2014 normal, due 2024.
- Prostate: discussed PSA pros and cons at 66; he does not want it.
- Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months.
- Pneumococcal: PCV20 with flu shot in October.
- Flu: high-dose in October.
- Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, urine albumin today.
- Advance directive: information packet given, he wants to think about it with his wife.

Follow up 3 months for DM.

documents.title: Your wellness visit labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Howard, the A1c came back 8.2, up from 6.8 in March. That's a real jump. Let's work on the bread and pasta piece you mentioned and recheck in a few months before thinking about another medicine. Kidney numbers, cholesterol, blood counts and urine albumin all stable. Your arm should be sore for a day or two from the shingles shot.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (high dose) 0.7 mL IM right deltoid. Prevnar 20 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Screened, no contraindications. VIS sheets for both. Observed 15 minutes without problem. He said the shingles shot gave him a sore arm and chills for a night; reminded him he still needs the second Shingrix, booked for December.

documents.title: Booster
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI had my Covid booster at the pharmacy last Wednesday the 27th, Pfizer again. -Howard Marino

documents.title: RE: Booster
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks! Added to your immunization record. See you December 7 for the second shingles shot.

documents.title: Shingrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second Shingrix 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Series complete. Pt tolerated, observed 15 min. Warned again about a sore arm/achy day. DM visit with PCP was rescheduled to March, labs then.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Interval: Last seen for AWV in Sept; A1c was 8.2 then. Says he and his wife 'went back to the old rules' after the holidays, smaller pasta portions, no juice. Weight up a little over the winter. Home BP fine. Walking most days. No chest pain, no breathing trouble.

Meds: ASA 81, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, metformin 1000 BID. No missed doses he can think of.

Exam: NAD. CV regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Ext no edema. Feet without lesions.

Assessment/plan
1. T2DM - recheck A1c, BMP. If still 7.5+ will talk about adding something.
2. CKD 3b - creatinine drifting? Will see today's value.
3. HTN - goal.
4. HLD/CAD - lipid today, statin.
5. Tdap today, last tetanus unknown.

Next in about 3 months.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 6.9, better. LDL 67. Creatinine 1.8, up slightly from 1.7, stays stage 3b. K normal. Continue current plan, repeat BMP in 6 months.

orders.reason: Exertional dyspnea and orthopnea in a patient with CAD after STEMI

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: getting winded.

HPI: Since mid-July has been short of breath on his walks, now stops halfway up the hill on his street that he used to do without a break. More tired in general. For the past few weeks has been sleeping on 3 pillows because he feels breathless flat; wife noticed. No chest pain or pressure, no palpitations, no fainting or near-fainting. No cough, fever, leg swelling he has noticed. No change in meds, taking all of them.

History: CAD with STEMI and DES 2016, HTN, DM2, HLD, CKD 3b. Has not seen cardiology since about 2017.

Exam: Sitting comfortably, speaks full sentences. BP and HR as recorded, SpO2 normal at rest. No JVD at 45 degrees. Heart RRR, no gallop. Lungs clear to bases. Abdomen soft. No ankle or leg edema.

A/P:
Exertional dyspnea and orthopnea, about 7 weeks, in a man with a prior MI. Worry about a cardiac cause, i.e. LV dysfunction or ischemia, even without angina.
- Cardiology referral, asked for the next available new consult with echo. Front desk to push for within 6 weeks.
- Start furosemide 40 mg every morning for the orthopnea in the meantime.
- BMP and CBC today, BMP again in 2 weeks on the diuretic.
- Precautions: chest pain, worsening breathlessness at rest, swelling, fainting -> call or 911.
RTC after cardiology.

documents.title: Lab result call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP, called patient: potassium and kidney function stable on the water pill, no change. Confirmed cardiology appointment Oct 19 at 1:30 with echo the same afternoon; he has the address and will bring his med list. He asked if he can keep taking the furosemide in the morning only, told him yes.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu high-dose IM R deltoid, COVID bivalent (Pfizer) IM L deltoid. Screening negative. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Pt says breathing 'about the same,' sleeping propped up; he has cardiology 10/19. Encouraged him to keep it.

conditions.label: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

reports.text:
Indication: exertional dyspnea, prior myocardial infarction.
Technically adequate study.
Left ventricle: dilated. Akinesis of the anterior wall and the septum. Remaining segments contract. Left ventricular ejection fraction 35%.
Right ventricle: normal size and systolic function.
Atria: normal size.
Valves: aortic valve trileaflet, opens normally. Mitral leaflets structurally normal. Tricuspid and pulmonic valves normal.
Pericardium: no effusion.
IVC: normal size with normal respiratory variation.
reports.conclusion: Dilated left ventricle with anterior and septal akinesis; LVEF 35%.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 78. Persistent ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads with deep Q waves.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm; anterior Q waves with persistent ST elevation.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 10/19/2022
Re: Howard Marino, DOB 01/19/1955

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Marino, a 67-year-old retired postal worker with coronary disease (STEMI 2016 treated with a drug-eluting stent), hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia and stage 3 kidney disease, about breathlessness.

Over roughly three months he has noticed steadily worsening shortness of breath with exertion and more fatigue, and he now needs to sleep propped up. He has had no chest pain, no palpitations and no syncope. You started furosemide in September.

Medications: aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: father with coronary disease and an MI at 62; mother diabetic and hypertensive; older brother with high cholesterol.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol. Retired from the postal service.

Exam: BP 130/80, heart rate 78, respiratory rate 20. On auscultation there is a holosystolic murmur at the apex that radiates to the axilla. Lungs are clear. No peripheral edema.

ECG: sinus rhythm with persistent anterior ST elevation and deep Q waves.
Echocardiogram today: the left ventricle is dilated, the anterior wall and septum are akinetic, and the ejection fraction is 35%.

Impression:
1. Ischemic cardiomyopathy with a left ventricular aneurysm involving the anterior wall and septum, the late result of his 2016 infarct.
2. Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
3. Coronary artery disease, stented 2016, no angina.

Plan: continue aspirin, metoprolol succinate, lisinopril, atorvastatin and furosemide as he takes them. Daily weights, 2 g sodium diet, call for a gain of more than 3 pounds in a day or 5 in a week. We will see him again in the spring.

Thank you for the referral.

Cardiology

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, subsequent.

Cardiology letter from 10/19 reviewed with him: echo shows a dilated LV with an akinetic anterior wall and septum, EF 35%, read as ischemic cardiomyopathy with an LV aneurysm from the 2016 MI, and HFrEF. Regimen continued as is. He understood it as 'the old heart attack left a weak spot.'

How he is doing: breathlessness on hills unchanged, sleeps on 2-3 pillows. Weighing himself every morning now, steady. Salt: wife has stopped using the shaker and they are reading labels.

HRA: lives with wife, independent, drives, no falls. PHQ-2 0. Mini-Cog normal last year, no concerns.

Meds: aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, metformin 1000 BID, furosemide 40 qAM.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Heart regular, no S3 heard today, apical systolic murmur noted as in the cardiology letter. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet intact, monofilament normal.

Plan:
- HFrEF/ICM: continue per cardiology. Daily weights, sodium limit. Reviewed when to call.
- DM2: A1c today.
- CKD 3b: CMP, urine albumin.
- HTN controlled.
- Prevention: flu and COVID done 10/4. Colonoscopy due 2024. PSA declined again. Shingrix, Tdap, PCV20 complete.
- Advance directive: still thinking.
RTC 3 months.
